title: Count prefixes, not information
hook: More symbols create more prefixes; do they reveal message probabilities?

doesNotKnow: Distinguish cumulative possibility count from probability-dependent entropy.

misconception: The number of possible messages alone determines their information.
objective: Distinguish cumulative possibility count from probability-dependent entropy.

claims.text: Communication models distinguish possible messages from their statistical uncertainty.
Claude E. Shannon and Warren Weaver, The Mathematical Theory of Communication (1949)
One round gives {A}; two give {B}. Each next symbol extends existing prefixes without collisions; the empty prefix counts once.
Does it hold up? This counts possibilities, not entropy. No symbol probabilities, noise model or coding theorem is supplied.

recall.question: The same four strings can be equally likely or very unequal. What is missing to compute entropy?
recall.why: Possibility counts do not specify the probabilities needed for entropy.
